328.subject: Botany
328.text:
Assertion : In angiosperms, transport of food and water is more efficient than gymnosperms and pteridophytes.
Reason : In angiosperms longitudinally arranged sieve elements and vessels with perforated end walls are present.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
328.sol:
Vessels are much elongated tubes which are closed at either end and are formed by the union of several short, wide and thickened cells called vessel elements. The end walls of vessel elements are transverse or oblique. They are often completely dissolved. The condition is called simple perforation plate. In a few cases the end walls remain intact and possess several pores in reticulate, scalariform or forminate forms. Such an end wall is called multiple perforation plate. Sieve tubes are elongated tubular conducting channels of phloem formed of several cells called sieve tube elements or members or sieve tube cells. Sieve tube members are placed end to end. The end walls are generally bulged out. They may be transverse or oblique. They have many small pores or sieve pits. Due to the presence of sieve pits the end walls are commonly called sieve plates. In some cases the end walls of sieve elements possess more than one porous area. Such an end wall is called compound sieve plate.
Gymnosperms \& pteridophytes lack these two vascular structures i.e. vessels and sieve elements. In angiosperms presence of vessels \& sieve elements in addition to all other vascular tissues make their food \& water transport more efficient.

2194.sol: A synapse occurs where the axon of one neuron (the pre-synaptic neuron) meets either the dendrite or the cell body of another (the post-synaptic neuron). At the tip of the pre-synaptic axon is a button shaped swelling called a synaptic knob, inside which are numerous mitochondria and vesicles packed with a substance called a neurotransmitter is present. This neurotransmitters at the time of nerve impulse diffuse across the space and bind to receptors in the membrane of the post-synaptic cell. This opens ion channels in the post-synaptic membrane of the postsynaptic cell resulting in a change in the post-synaptic cell's membrane potential and (if the cell is sufficiently excited) in the consequent generation of a nerve impulse.

2208.subject: Zoology
2208.text: At a particular locus, frequency of allele ' $A$ ' is 0.6 and that of allele ' $a$ ' is 0.4 . What would be the frequency of heterozygotes in a random mating population at equilibrium?
2208.sol:
In a stable population, for a gene with two alleles, ' A$ ' (dominant) and 'a' (recessive), if the frequency of ' A$ ' is $p$ and the frequency of ' $\mathrm{a}$ ' is $q$, then the frequencies of the three possible genotypes (AA, Aa and aa) can be expressed by the Hardy-Weinberg equation:
$p^2+2 p q+q^2=1$
where $p^2=$ Frequency of AA (homozygous dominant) individuals
$q^2=$ Frequency of aa (homozygous recessive) individuals
$2 p q=$ Frequency of Aa (heterozygous) individuals.
So, $p=0.6 and q=0.4$ (given)
$\begin{aligned} \therefore 2 p q(\text{ frequency$ of $heterozygote }) & =2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 \\ & =0.48 .\end{aligned}$

\end{aligned}$
Hence, $\mathrm{K}_{3} \left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right] will be most effective in causing coagulation of ferric hydroxide solution.$

Identify the correct statements from the following.

III. Gibb's energy is a state function.
5948.sol:
At $0 \mathrm{ K}$, the entropy of pure crystalline materials is zero.
$\therefore$ The statement (I) is correct as entropy approach zero, at absolute zero.
Statement (II) entropy for the process,
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l) \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$ decreases is incorrect as entropy increases. The degree of randomness when water vaporises to gaseous state increases.
(III) Gibbs' energy is a state function is correct as the Gibbs' free energy depends on initial and final state only.
Hence, statement (I) and (III) are correct.

8591.text: If tangents are drawn to the ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{5} = 1$ at the ends of latus recta, then the area of the quadrilateral thus formed is
8591.sol:
The given equation of the ellipse is,

$\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{5} = 1$

The eccentricity of the ellipse is,

$e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{5}{9}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

The coordinates of the endpoints of latus rectum are

$L\left(2, \dfrac{5}{3}\right), M\left(- 2, \dfrac{5}{3}\right), {M}^{'}\left(- 2, \dfrac{- 5}{3}\right)$ and ${L}^{'}\left(2, \dfrac{- 5}{3}\right)$

The equations of tangents at these points are,

$2x + 3y - 9 = 0$
$- 2x + 3y - 9 = 0$
$2x + 3y + 9 = 0$
$- 2x + 3y + 9 = 0$

By solving the above equations,

$A\left(0, 3\right)$

$B\left(- \dfrac{9}{2}, 0\right)$

$C\left(0, - 3\right)$
$D\left(\dfrac{9}{2}, 0\right)$

And
$AC = \sqrt{( 3 + 3{)}^{2}} = 6$

$BD = \sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{9}{2} + \dfrac{9}{2}\right)}^{2}} = 9$

The area of the quadrilateral is,
$A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 6$

$= 27sq . units$

11520.text: The condition that the roots of $x^3-b x^2+c x-d=0$ are in geometric progression is
11520.sol:
Equation, $x^3-b x^2+c x-d=0$
Let the roots of this cubic equation in GP are $\left(\frac{a}{r}, a, a r\right)$
Then, Sum of the roots
$\frac{a}{r}+a+a r=-\left(\frac{-b}{1}\right) \Rightarrow b\Rightarrow \quad a\left(\frac{1}{r}+1+r\right)=b\ldots$ (i)
and $\quad \frac{a}{r} \cdot a+a \cdot a r+a r \cdot \frac{a}{r}=\frac{c}{1}\Rightarrow \quad a^2\left(\frac{1}{r}+r+1\right)=c\ldots$ (ii)
Product of the roots
$\frac{a}{r} \cdot a \cdot a r=-\left(\frac{-d}{1}\right)=d\Rightarrow \quad a^3=d\ldots$ (iii)
Eq. (ii) divided by Eq. (i), we get $a=c / b$, put the value of ' $a$ ' in Eq. (iii)
$(c / b)^3=d\Rightarrow \quad c^3=b^3 d$

12480.text: Two lines whose direction cosines are given by $a l+b m+c n=0$ and $f m n+g n l+h l m=0$ are perpendicular to each other if.........
12480.sol:
Let the direction cosines of lines are $l_1, m_1, n_1$ and $l_2, m_2, n_2$
Since, $a l+b m+c n=0$ and, $f m n+g n l+h m=0$
So, on eliminating ' $l$ ', we get

$\begin{gathered}$f m n+(g n+h m)$\left(-\frac{b m+c n}{a}\right)=$0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad a f m n=b h m²+c g n²+(b g+c h) m n=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad b h$\left(\frac{m}{n}\right)^$2+(b g+c h-a f)$\left(\frac{m}{n}\right)+$c g=0 $\text{ having }$\\
$\text{ roots } \frac{m_1}{n_1} \text{ and } \frac{m_2}{n_2} \text{, so }$\\
$\text{ product of roots }=\frac{m_1 m_2}{n_1 n_2}=\frac{c g}{b h}
\end{gathered}$Similarly on eliminating ' $m$ ', we get

$\begin{gathered}$g n l+(h l+f n)$\left(-\frac{a l+c n}{b}\right)=$0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad b g n l=a h l²+c f n²+(c h+a f) l n=0 \\
\Rightarrow a h$\left(\frac{l}{n}\right)^$2+(c h+a f-b g)$\left(\frac{l}{n}\right)+$c f=0 $\text{, having roots }$\\
$\frac{l_1}{n_1} \text{ and } \frac{l_2}{n_2} \text{, so product of roots } \frac{l_1 l_2}{n_1 n_2}=\frac{c f}{a h} .
\end{gathered}\because$ The lines are perpendicular.

$\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore$& l_1 l_2+m_1 m_2+n_1 n_2=0 \\
\Rightarrow & $\left(\frac{c g}{b h}+\frac{c f}{a h}+$1\right) n_1 n_2=0 \Rightarrow $\frac{f}{a}+\frac{g}{b}+\frac{h}{c}=$0
\end{array}

14510.text: Four charges, each charge $q$ coulomb are placed at points $(-1,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,-1,0)$ and $(0,1,0)$ in the $x y$-plane. The distance along the axes are measured in metres. The magnitude of the electric field at the point $z=1 \mathrm{ m}$ on the $Z$-axis is
14510.sol:
The given situation is shown below.
According to given situation we have to find electric field at point $P(0,0,1)$. Distance of point $P$ from each charges is equal to $\begin{aligned} \sqrt{1^2+1^2}$& =$\sqrt{2}$\\ E_{A P} & =E_{B P}=E_{C P}=E_{D P}=$\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q}{(\sqrt{2})^2}$\\ & =$\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q}{2} \end{aligned}E_{A P}$ and $E_{B P}$ are perpendicular to each other. Let $E^{\prime}$ be the resultant electric field of $E_{A P}$ and $E_{B P}$, then $\begin{array}{rlr}$ E^{\prime} & =$\sqrt{E_{A P}^2+E_{B P}^2}=\sqrt{2 E_{A P}^2} \quad\left[\because$ E_{A P}=E_{B P}\right] \\ & =E_{A P} $\sqrt{2}$\\ & =$\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q \sqrt{2}}{2}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q}{\sqrt{2}}$\\ E^{\prime} & =$\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q}{\sqrt{2}} \end{array}$ In the similar way, net electric field due to $E_{C P}$ and $E_{D P}$ E^{\prime \prime}=$\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q}{\sqrt{2}}$ Again $E^{\prime}$ and $E^{\prime \prime}$ are directed in same direction i.e along $+z$ direction, hence net electric field, $\begin{aligned} E_{\mathrm{net}$} & =E^{\prime}+E^{\prime \prime}=2 E^{\prime} \\ & =2 $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{q}{2 \sqrt{2} \pi \varepsilon_0} \mathrm{ N}$/ $\mathrm{C} \end{aligned}$

16442.text: In a \(p\)-type semiconductor the donor level is at \(50 \mathrm{meV}\) above the valence band. To produce one electron, the maximum wavelength of light photon required is (Planck's constant, \(h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\) and speed of light in vacuum, \(c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}\) )
16442.sol:
Given,
\(p\)-type semiconductor donor energy level,
\(E=50 \mathrm{meV}=50 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~V}\)
Planck's constant, \(h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\)
speed of light in vacuum, \(c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\)
Now, for the maximum wavelength of light photon's required \((p)\).
According to the Planck's quantum theory,
\(\therefore \quad E=h v \Rightarrow E=\frac{h c}{\lambda} \quad\left[\because v=\frac{c}{\lambda}\right]\)
Putting the given values, we get
\(50 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}=\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{\lambda}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\lambda & =\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{50 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \\
& =\frac{6.6 \times 3 \times 10^{-34} \times 10^8}{5 \times 16 \times 10^{-22}}=\frac{6.6 \times 3 \times 10^{-4}}{5 \times 16} \\
& =2.475 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~m} \\
\text{or } \lambda & =24.75 \times 10^{-6}=24.75 \mu \mathrm{m}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, the maximum wavelength of light photon required is \(24.8 \mu \mathrm{m}\).

19604.subject: Chemistry
options: Anilinium ion is less resonance stabilised than Aniline.
Aliphatic amines are weaker bases than $\mathrm{NH}_3$ while aromatic amines are stronger bases than $\mathrm{NH}_3$.
Sec-butylamine is optically inactive because Nitrogen atom of the $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group is achiral.
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for preparing both Ethyl amine and Aniline.
19604.sol:
(1) Correct: In aniline (C_6H_5NH_2$), the lone pair on N is delocalized into the benzene ring, forming multiple resonance structures. In the anilinium ion (C_6H_5NH_3^+$), the lone pair is donated to a proton and can no longer participate in resonance. Hence anilinium ion is less resonance stabilised than aniline.

(2) Incorrect: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than $NH_3$ due to the $+I$ effect of alkyl groups. Aromatic amines are weaker bases than $NH_3$ because their lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring.

(3) Incorrect: sec-Butylamine (CH_3CH_2CH(NH_2)CH_3$) has a chiral carbon bonded to four different groups ($-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH_2CH_3$, $-NH_2$), making it optically active.

(4) Incorrect: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves $S_N2$ reaction with alkyl halides. Aryl halides do not undergo $S_N2$, so aniline cannot be prepared by this method.

The correct statement is (1).$

19901.text: At $300 \mathrm{ K}$, the half-life period of a gaseous reaction at an initial pressure of $40 \mathrm{kPa}$ is 350 s. When pressure is $20 \mathrm{kPa}$, the half-life period is $175 \mathrm{ s}$. What is the order of the reaction?

We know that
$\frac{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_1}{\left(t_{1 / 2}\right)_2}=\left(\frac{p_2}{p_1}\right)^{n-1}$
where, $n$ is the order of reaction and $t_{1 / 2}$ is half-life.
$\begin{gathered}
\frac{350}{175}=\left(\frac{20}{40}\right)^{n-1} \\
2=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1} \\
\Rightarrow n-1=-1 \\
n=0
\end{gathered}\therefore$ It is a zero order reaction.

20068.subject: Chemistry
20068.text: Larger number of oxidation states are exhibited by the actinoids than those of lanthanoids. The reason is:
options: Highly reactive nature of the actinoids
More energy difference between 5f and 6d than between 4f and 5d orbitals
4f orbitals are more diffused than 5f orbitals
Lesser energy difference between 5f and 6d than between 4f and 5d orbitals
20068.sol:
Lanthanoids exhibit primarily the +3 oxidation state because the 4f orbitals are deeply buried within the atom and are shielded by the 5s and 5p orbitals, making them less available for bonding. The energy gap between the 4f and 5d orbitals is relatively large, which restricts the participation of 4f electrons in chemical bonding.

In contrast, the actinoids exhibit a wider range of oxidation states (such as +3, +4, +5, +6, and +7). This is because the 5f orbitals in actinoids are not as deeply buried as the 4f orbitals in lanthanoids. Furthermore, the energy difference between the 5f, 6d, and 7s orbitals is significantly smaller than the energy difference between the 4f, 5d, and 6s orbitals in lanthanoids. This smaller energy gap allows the 5f electrons to participate more readily in bonding, leading to a greater variety of oxidation states.

Answer: Lesser energy difference between 5f and 6d than between 4f and 5d orbitals

20394.text:
Convert Benzene → 3-Bromophenol by choosing appropriate reagents $[(i)$ to (v)] in the correct sequence.
$(i)\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}\left(0^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\right) \quad (ii) Conc. \mathrm{HNO}_3 / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \quad (iii) \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} / 283 \mathrm{ K} \quad (iv) \mathrm{Fe} / \mathrm{HCl} \quad (v) \mathrm{Br} 2 / \mathrm{Fe}$
20394.sol:
The conversion of benzene to 3-bromophenol requires the introduction of a meta-directing group followed by bromination, or the use of a group that directs meta and can be converted to a hydroxyl group. Since the hydroxyl group is ortho/para-directing, it must be introduced after the bromine atom is placed in the meta position.

Nitration of benzene using $Conc. HNO_3 / H_2SO_4$ (reagent ii) gives nitrobenzene.

Bromination of nitrobenzene using $Br_2 / Fe$ (reagent v) gives 1-bromo-3-nitrobenzene because the nitro group is meta-directing.

Reduction of the nitro group using $Fe / HCl$ (reagent iv) gives 3-bromoaniline.

Diazotization of 3-bromoaniline using $NaNO_2 / HCl$ at $0^{{}^{\circ}}C$ (reagent i) gives 3-bromobenzenediazonium chloride.

Hydrolysis of the diazonium salt using $H_2O / 283 K$ (reagent iii) gives 3-bromophenol.

The correct sequence is ii, v, iv, i, iii.

Answer: ii, v, iv, i, iii

20667.text: If the depression in freezing point of an aqueous solution containing a solute, which is neither dissociated nor associated, is $\mathrm{a} \mathrm{K}$ with $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}=\mathrm{b K k g m o l}{ }^{-1}$, what would be the elevation in boiling point $(\mathrm{X})$ for this solution if its $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}=\mathrm{\mathrm { K } \mathrm { K } \mathrm { kg } \mathrm { mol }}{ }^{-1}$ ?
20667.sol:
The depression in freezing point is given by the formula $\Delta T_f = K_f \times m$, where $m$ is the molality of the solution. Given $\Delta T_f = a$ and $K_f = b$, we have $a = b \times m$, which implies $m = \dfrac{a}{b}$.

The elevation in boiling point is given by the formula $\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$, where $K_b = c$. Substituting the value of $m$ obtained from the freezing point depression, we get $\Delta T_b = c \times \dfrac{a}{b}$.

Therefore, $X = c \times \dfrac{a}{b}$.

Answer: $X=c \times \dfrac{a}{b}$

21358.text: $The solution of the differential equation \dfrac{d y}{d x}+\sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}}=0$ is
21358.sol:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}} = 0$.

Separating the variables, we get $\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}} = -\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.

Integrating both sides, we have $\int \dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}} = -\int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.

Using the standard integral $\int \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^2}} = \sin^{-1} t + C$, we obtain $\sin^{-1} y = -\sin^{-1} x + C$.

Rearranging the terms, we get $\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y = C$.

Answer: $\sin ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} y=c$

21939.subject: Mathematics
21939.text: Three vertices are chosen randomly from the seven vertices of a regular 7 -sided polygon. The probability that they form the vertices of an isosceles triangle is
21939.sol:
The total number of ways to choose 3 vertices out of 7 is given by $^{7}C_{3} = \dfrac{7 \times 6 \times 5}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 35$.

An isosceles triangle is formed if at least two sides of the triangle are equal. In a regular 7-sided polygon, let the vertices be $V_{0}, V_{1}, V_{2}, V_{3}, V_{4}, V_{5}, V_{6}$.

For any vertex chosen as the apex of the isosceles triangle, there are 3 possible pairs of other vertices that form an isosceles triangle with it. For example, if $V_{0}$ is the apex, the pairs are $(V_{1}, V_{6})$, $(V_{2}, V_{5})$, and $(V_{3}, V_{4})$.

Since there are 7 vertices, and each vertex can serve as the apex for 3 distinct isosceles triangles, the total number of isosceles triangles is $7 \times 3 = 21$.

The probability is the ratio of the number of isosceles triangles to the total number of triangles: $P = \dfrac{21}{35} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{5}$

22009.subject: Mathematics
22009.text: The value of $\dfrac{1}{2 !}+\dfrac{2}{3 !}+$\ldots+$\dfrac{99}{100 !} is equal to$
22009.sol:
The general term of the series is $T_n = \dfrac{n}{(n+1)!}$ for $n = 1, 2, \ldots, 99$.

We can rewrite the general term as $T_n = \dfrac{n+1-1}{(n+1)!} = \dfrac{n+1}{(n+1)!} - \dfrac{1}{(n+1)!} = \dfrac{1}{n!} - \dfrac{1}{(n+1)!}$.

The sum $S$ is given by $\sum_{n=1}^{99} \left( \dfrac{1}{n!} - \dfrac{1}{(n+1)!} \right).

This is a telescoping series:

$ S = $\left( \dfrac{1}{1!} - \dfrac{1}{2!} \right)$+ $\left( \dfrac{1}{2!} - \dfrac{1}{3!} \right)$+ \ldots + $\left( \dfrac{1}{99!} - \dfrac{1}{100!} \right)$.

All intermediate terms cancel out, leaving $S = \dfrac{1}{1!} - \dfrac{1}{100!} =1 - \dfrac{1}{100!}.

$ S = $\dfrac{100! - 1}{100!}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{100 !-1}{100 !}$

22799.subject: Physics
22799.text: Two conducting spherical shells A and B of radii 4 cm and 6 cm respectively are placed with their centres 17 cm apart in air. Initially, sphere A was given a $-20$ nC charge while sphere B was uncharged. The spheres are then connected by a long thin conducting wire and allowed to reach electrostatic equilibrium. Assuming no charge is lost to the surroundings, the final charge on sphere A and the ratio of magnitude of electric field intensity at the surface of sphere B to that of sphere A is given by:
22799.sol:
When the two conducting spheres are connected by a long thin conducting wire, charge flows until their electrostatic potentials become equal. Assuming the distance between them is sufficient to ignore mutual potential effects, the potential of each sphere is given by $V = \dfrac{kq}{R}$.

Equating the potentials of sphere A and sphere B:
$V_A = V_B$
$\dfrac{k q_A}{R_A} = \dfrac{k q_B}{R_B}$
$\dfrac{q_A}{4} = \dfrac{q_B}{6} \Rightarrow q_B = \dfrac{3}{2} q_A$

According to the conservation of charge, the total initial charge equals the total final charge:
$q_A + q_B = -20\text{ nC}$
$q_A + \dfrac{3}{2} q_A = -20\text{ nC}$
$\dfrac{5}{2} q_A = -20\text{ nC} \Rightarrow q_A = -8\text{ nC}$

The magnitude of the electric field intensity at the surface of a conducting sphere is $E = \dfrac{kq}{R^2}$.

The ratio of the electric field at the surface of sphere B to that of sphere A is:
$\dfrac{E_B}{E_A} = \dfrac{\dfrac{k q_B}{R_B^2}}{\dfrac{k q_A}{R_A^2}} = \left(\dfrac{q_B}{q_A}\right) \left(\dfrac{R_A}{R_B}\right)^2$

Since $\dfrac{q_B}{q_A} = \dfrac{R_B}{R_A}$, we get:
$\dfrac{E_B}{E_A} = \left(\dfrac{R_B}{R_A}\right) \left(\dfrac{R_A}{R_B}\right)^2 = \dfrac{R_A}{R_B}$

Substituting the given radii:
$\dfrac{E_B}{E_A} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Answer: $-8\text{nC}\ ;\ \dfrac{2}{3}$

22911.text: If $\mathrm{A}$ is the areal velocity of a planet of mass $\mathrm{M}$, then its angular momentum is
22911.sol:
The areal velocity of a planet is defined as the rate at which the area is swept by the radius vector, given by $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2} r^2 \dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$.

The angular momentum $L$ of a planet of mass $M$ moving in an orbit is given by $L = mvr = mr^2 \omega$, where $\omega = \dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$.

Substituting $\omega$ into the expression for angular momentum, we get $L = M r^2 \dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$.

Comparing this with the expression for areal velocity $A = \dfrac{1}{2} r^2 \dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$, we see that $r^2 \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = 2A$.

Therefore, $L = M(2A) = 2MA$.

Answer: $2 \mathrm{MA}$

Therefore, $\chi \propto \dfrac{1}{T}$.

23272.text: $\text{ If the nuclear radius of }{ }^{27} \mathrm{Al} \text{ is } 3.6 \text{ fermi, the nuclear radius of }{ }^{125} \mathrm{Fe} \text{$ is }
23272.sol:
The nuclear radius $R$ is given by the formula $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant and $A$ is the mass number of the nucleus.

For $^{27}\mathrm{Al}$, the mass number $A_1 = 27$ and the radius $R_1 = 3.6 \text{ fermi}$.

Using the formula, $3.6 = R_0 (27)^{1/3} = R_0 \times 3$, which gives $R_0 = 1.2 \text{ fermi}$.

For $^{125}\mathrm{Fe}$, the mass number $A_2 = 125$. The radius $R_2$ is given by $R_2 = R_0 (125)^{1/3} = 1.2 \times 5 = 6.0 \text{ fermi}$.

Since $1 \text{ fermi} = 10^{-15} \text{ m}$, the radius $R_2 = 6.0 \times 10^{-15} \text{ m}$.

Answer: $6 \times 10^{-15} \mathrm{~m}$

\Rightarrow \quad &\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{-0.5}=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{1.5}\\

\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{p_{1}}{p_{2}}=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{\frac{15}{05}}=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{3}=\frac{1}{27}\Rightarrow \quad p_{2}=27 p_{1}=27 \times 1 \times 10^{5}=27 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{ N} / \mathrmm^{2}$

24472.subject: Chemistry
24472.text:
In the following reaction sequence, $\textbf{P}$, $\textbf{Q}$, $\textbf{S}$ and $\textbf{T}$ are the major products.

The correct statement(s) about $\textbf{P}$, $\textbf{Q}$, $\textbf{S}$ and $\textbf{T}$ is(are)
options: $\textbf{Q}$ on treatment with ethanol generates an aromatic aldehyde.
24472.sol:
In the first reaction sequence:
Step 1: Aniline reacts with acetic anhydride in the presence of pyridine to undergo acetylation, forming acetanilide.
Step 2: Acetanilide is treated with a nitrating mixture (conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) at $288 \text{ K}$. The $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group is moderately activating and ortho/para directing. Due to steric hindrance, the major product $\textbf{P}$ is $p$-nitroacetanilide.
Step 3: $\textbf{P}$ is hydrolyzed with $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ to yield $p$-nitroaniline.
Step 4: $p$-nitroaniline is diazotized using $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $273-278 \text{ K}$ to form the diazonium salt $\textbf{Q}$, which is $p$-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride.

In the second reaction sequence:
Step 1: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidized by $\text{O}_2$ followed by acid hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) to produce phenol and acetone. The major aromatic product is phenol.
Step 2: Phenol undergoes the Kolbe-Schmitt reaction with $\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{CO}_2$ to form sodium salicylate.
Step 3: Acidification with $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ yields salicylic acid as the major product $\textbf{S}$.

In the final reaction:
Salicylic acid ($\textbf{S}$) reacts with $p$-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride ($\textbf{Q}$) in an aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ medium. This is an electrophilic aromatic substitution (azo coupling). The phenoxide ion formed is highly activating, and coupling occurs at the para position with respect to the $-\text{OH}$ group (position 5 of salicylic acid). The resulting product $\textbf{T}$ is an azo dye, which is a highly conjugated and coloured compound.

Evaluating the options:
(A) Treatment of $\textbf{Q}$ ($p$-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride) with ethanol reduces the diazonium group, yielding nitrobenzene, not an aromatic aldehyde. (Incorrect)
(B) The phthalein dye test is a characteristic test for phenols. Salicylic acid ($\textbf{S}$) contains a phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group with a free para position (position 5) and gives a positive phthalein dye test when heated with phthalic anhydride and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. (Correct)
(C) $\textbf{P}$ is $p$-nitroacetanilide, which is a mononitro compound, not a dinitro compound. (Incorrect)
(D) $\textbf{T}$ is an azo dye, which is a coloured compound. (Correct)

Answer: $\textbf{S}$ gives positive phthalein dye test.; $\textbf{T}$ is a coloured compound.

28201.text: For a reversible reaction $A ⇌ B$, the $∆ H$ forward reaction $= 20kJ{mol}^{– 1}$. The activation energy of the uncatalyzed forward reaction is $300kJ{mol}^{– 1}$. The activation energy of the catalysed backward reaction is _______$kJ{mol}^{– 1}$.
28201.sol:
As per the question

To determine the activation energy of the catalyzed backward reaction, we need to use the Arrhenius equation and the given information.

The Arrhenius equation is given by:

$k = {Ae}^{( - Ea / RT )}$

${Ae}^{- \dfrac{300 \times {10}^{3}}{600 \times R}} = Ae\dfrac{- Ea}{300 \times R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{10}^{3}}{2} = \dfrac{Ea}{300}$

$⇒ {E}_{a} = 150 \times {10}^{3}J{mol}^{– 1}$

$⇒ {E}_{a} = 150kJ{mol}^{– 1}$

$∴$ Activation energy of catalysed backward reaction

Energy of activation for backward reaction${E}_{b} = {E}_{a} - ∆ H$

$= 150 - 20 = 130kJ{mol}^{– 1}$

The standard cell potential is given by:
$E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{cathode} - E^\circ_{anode} = 0.80 - (-0.76) = 1.56\text{ V}$

Using the Nernst equation:
$E_{cell} = E^\circ_{cell} - \dfrac{0.059}{n} \log \dfrac{[Zn^{2+}]}{[Ag^+]^2}$

Substituting the given values ($n = 2$, $[Zn^{2+}] = 1\text{ M}$, $E_{cell} = 1.60\text{ V}$):
$1.60 = 1.56 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \log \dfrac{1}{x^2}$

$0.04 = - \dfrac{0.059}{2} (-2 \log x)$

$0.04 = 0.059 \log x$

$\log x = \dfrac{0.04}{0.059} = \dfrac{4}{5.9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{5.9}$

32154.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I
Orbital		List-II
Radial nodes and nodal plane
A. $2s$I. $1$ Radial node + two nodal planes
B. $3s$II. $1$ Radial node + one nodal plane

D. $4d$IV. $1$ Radial node + No nodal plane

32154.sol:
The number of radial nodes is given by the formula $n - l - 1$.

The number of nodal planes (angular nodes) is given by $l$.

Radial nodes = $2 - 0 - 1 = 1$.
Nodal planes = $0$.
This matches A with IV.

For $3s$ orbital: $n = 3$, $l = 0$.
Radial nodes = $3 - 0 - 1 = 2$.
Nodal planes = $0$.
This matches B with III.

For $3p$ orbital: $n = 3$, $l = 1$.
Radial nodes = $3 - 1 - 1 = 1$.
Nodal planes = $1$.
This matches C with II.

For $4d$ orbital: $n = 4$, $l = 2$.
Radial nodes = $4 - 2 - 1 = 1$.
Nodal planes = $2$.
This matches D with I.

The correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

32798.subject: Mathematics
32798.text:
Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f''(x) > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R} and f'(a-1) = 0$, where $a$ is a real number. Let $g(x) = f\left( \tan^{2}x - 2\tan x + a \right), \; 0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2}$.

Consider the following two statements:
(I) $g$ is increasing in $\left(0, \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
(II) $g$ is decreasing in $\left(\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Then,
32798.sol:
Given $f''(x) > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, which means $f'(x)$ is a strictly increasing function.
We are given $f'(a-1) = 0$. Since $f'(x)$ is strictly increasing, $f'(x) < 0$ for $x < a-1$ and $f'(x) > 0$ for $x > a-1$.
The function $g(x)$ is defined as $g(x) = f(\tan^2 x - 2\tan x + a)$ for $x \in (0, \pi/2)$.
Let $u(x) = \tan^2 x - 2\tan x + a = (\tan x - 1)^2 + a - 1$.
Differentiating $g(x)$ with respect to $x$:
$g'(x) = f'(u(x)) \cdot u'(x) = f'((\tan x - 1)^2 + a - 1) \cdot (2\tan x \sec^2 x - 2\sec^2 x)$
$g'(x) = f'((\tan x - 1)^2 + a - 1) \cdot 2\sec^2 x (\tan x - 1)$.

Case 1: $x \in (0, \pi/4)$.
In this interval, $0 < \tan x < 1$, so $(\tan x - 1) < 0$.
Also, $(\tan x - 1)^2 > 0$, so $u(x) = (\tan x - 1)^2 + a - 1 > a - 1$.
Since $f'(x)$ is increasing and $f'(a-1) = 0$, for $u(x) > a - 1$, we have $f'(u(x)) > 0$.
Thus, $g'(x) = (+)(+)(-) < 0$. So $g(x)$ is decreasing in $(0, \pi/4)$.
Statement (I) is False.

Case 2: $x \in (\pi/4, \pi/2)$.
In this interval, $\tan x > 1$, so $(\tan x - 1) > 0$.
Also, $(\tan x - 1)^2 > 0$, so $u(x) = (\tan x - 1)^2 + a - 1 > a - 1$.
Thus, $f'(u(x)) > 0$.
Then $g'(x) = (+)(+)(+) > 0$. So $g(x)$ is increasing in $(\pi/4, \pi/2)$.
Statement (II) is False.

Therefore, neither (I) nor (II) is true.

33796.text: If $z = x + iy, xy \ne 0$, satisfies the equation ${z}^{2} + i\overset{¯}{z} = 0$, then $\left|{z}^{2}\right|$ is equal to :
33796.sol:
Given: ${z}^{2} + i z = 0$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = - i z$

Now taking $z = x + iy$ we get,

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2ixy = - ix - y$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} = - y \text{ and } 2xy = - x$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} = - y \text{ and } x\left(2y + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)}^{2} = - \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \text{ and } y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

Hence, $z = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + i\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} \pm 2i\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {z}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \pm i\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left|{z}^{2}\right| = {\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}}\right)}^{2} = 1$

36331.subject: Mathematics
36331.text: Let $p_n$ denote the total number of triangles formed by joining the vertices of an $n$-side regular polygon. If $p_{n+1} - p_n = 66$, then the sum of all distinct prime divisors of $n$ is:
36331.sol:
The number of triangles formed by joining the vertices of an $n$-sided regular polygon is given by $p_n = ^{n}C_{3}$.

Given that $p_{n+1} - p_n = 66$.

$^{n+1}C_{3} - ^{n}C_{3} = 66$

Using the property $^{n+1}C_{r} - ^{n}C_{r} = ^{n}C_{r-1}$, we get:

$^{n}C_{2} = 66$

$\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2} = 66$

$n(n-1) = 132$

$n^2 - n - 132 = 0$

$(n-12)(n+11) = 0$

Since $n$ must be a positive integer, $n = 12$.

The prime factorization of $12$ is $2^2 \times 3$. The distinct prime divisors of $12$ are $2$ and $3$.

The sum of all distinct prime divisors of $n$ is $2 + 3 = 5$.

Answer: $5$

38501.text: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$ be three vectors such that $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}$. If the angle between the vector $\overset{\to}{c}$ and the vector $3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is $\theta$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $\tan^{2}\theta$ is:
38501.sol:
Given: $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + k$, $\overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}k$

Also, $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{a} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c} = \lambda\overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2k = \left(4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}k\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + k\right)$

$⇒ \lambda + 4 = - 1, \lambda + {c}_{2} = - 8, \lambda + {c}_{3} = 2$

$⇒ \lambda = - 5, {c}_{2} = - 3, {c}_{3} = 7$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7k$

Now, finding angle we get,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\left(3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\left|\left(3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\right| ⋅ \left|\left(4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right)\right|}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{12 - 12 + 7}{\sqrt{26} ⋅ \sqrt{74}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{26} ⋅ \sqrt{74}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{7}{2\sqrt{481}}$

$⇒ sec\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{481}}{7}$

$⇒ {sec}^{2}\theta = \dfrac{4 \times 481}{49}$

$⇒ 1 + \tan^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1924}{49}$

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1875}{49}$

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta \approx 38 . 26$

$⇒ \left[\tan^{2}\theta\right] = \left[38 . 26\right] = 38$

38749.text: The electric current in the circuit is given as $i=i_{\mathrm{o}}(t / T)$. The r.m.s current for the period $t=0$ to $t=T$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
38749.sol:
The RMS current is calculated using $I_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T i^2 dt}$.
Given $i = i_0(t/T)$:
$I_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T i_0^2\left(\frac{t}{T}\right)^2 dt} = \sqrt{\frac{i_0^2}{T^3}\int_0^T t^2 dt} = \sqrt{\frac{i_0^2}{T^3} \cdot \frac{T^3}{3}}$
$= \sqrt{\frac{i_0^2}{3}} = \frac{i_0}{\sqrt{3}}$.

Therefore: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{3mkT}}$

$\lambda = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{6.62 \times 10^{-46}}} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}{2.57 \times 10^{-23}}$
$\lambda = 2.58 \times 10^{-11}$ m $= 25.8 \times 10^{-12}$ m, so $x \approx 26$

40583.text: Two identical charged particles each having a mass $10g$ and charge $2 . 0 \times {10}^{- 7}C$ are placed on a horizontal table with a separation of $L$ between them such that they stay in limited equilibrium. If the coefficient of friction between each particle and the table is $0 . 25$, find the value of $L$. [Use $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$ ]
40583.sol:
Normal reaction applied by table on object will be, $N = mg$.

Both charges are same, hence a repulsive force will act between them.

Value of force acting will be, $\dfrac{k{Q}^{2}}{{L}^{2}}$.

Now the maximum value of friction force which table can provide is,

$= \muN = \mumg$

For equilibrium, $\dfrac{k{Q}^{2}}{{L}^{2}} = \mumg$.

$L = \sqrt{\dfrac{k{Q}^{2}}{\mumg}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{0 . 25mg}}Q = 2\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{mg}}Q$

$= 2\sqrt{\dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9}}{10 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 10}}\left(2 \times {10}^{- 7}\right) = 0 . 12m = 12cm$

41408.subject: Physics
41408.text: A particle having charge $10^{-9}$ C moving in $x$-$y$ plane in fields of $0.4\hat{j}$ N/C and $4 \times 10^{-3} \hat{k}$ T experiences a force of $(4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) \times 10^{-10}$ N. The velocity of the particle at that instant is _______ m/s.
41408.sol:
The Lorentz force experienced by a charged particle is given by $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.

Given that the particle moves in the $x$-$y$ plane, its velocity can be written as $\vec{v} = v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j}$.

Substituting the given values into the force equation:

$\vec{F} = 10^{-9} [0.4\hat{j} + (v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j}) \times (4 \times 10^{-3} \hat{k})]$

Using the cross product rules $\hat{i} \times \hat{k} = -\hat{j}$ and $\hat{j} \times \hat{k} = \hat{i}$:

$\vec{F} = 10^{-9} [0.4\hat{j} - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x \hat{j} + 4 \times 10^{-3} v_y \hat{i}]$

$\vec{F} = 10^{-9} [4 \times 10^{-3} v_y \hat{i} + (0.4 - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x) \hat{j}]$

The given force is $\vec{F} = (4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) \times 10^{-10}$ N, which can be rewritten as:

$\vec{F} = 10^{-9} (0.4\hat{i} + 0.2\hat{j})$ N

Comparing the coefficients of $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ from both expressions:

For the $\hat{i}$ component:
$4 \times 10^{-3} v_y = 0.4$
$v_y = \dfrac{0.4}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = 100$ m/s

For the $\hat{j}$ component:
$0.4 - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x = 0.2$
$4 \times 10^{-3} v_x = 0.2$
$v_x = \dfrac{0.2}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = 50$ m/s

Therefore, the velocity of the particle is $\vec{v} = 50\hat{i} + 100\hat{j}$ m/s.

Answer: $50\hat{i} + 100\hat{j}$

44644.text: A stone tide to a string of length $L$ is whirled in a vertical circle with the other end of the string at the centre. At a certain instant of time, the stone is at its lowest position and has a speed $u$. The magnitude of change in its velocity, as it reaches a position where the string is horizontal, is $\sqrt{x\left({u}^{2} - gL\right)}$. The value of $x$ is
44644.sol:
Applying conservation of mechanical energy at the point $A and B$, we get$\dfrac{1}{2}m{u}^{2} + 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + mgL$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{{u}^{2} - 2gL}$

Now in vector form. $\overset{\to}{v}i = u\overset{^}{i} and \overset{\to}{v}f = v\overset{^}{j}$

Therefore, change in velocity will be,$∆ \overset{\to}{V} = v\overset{^}{j} - u\overset{^}{i} and \left|\Delta\overset{\to}{V}\right| = \sqrt{{u}^{2} + {v}^{2}}$

$⇒ \DeltaV = \sqrt{{u}^{2} + \left({u}^{2} - 2gL\right)}$

$= \sqrt{2\left({u}^{2} - gL\right)}$

Hence, $x = 2$

44925.subject: Botany
44925.sol: The shape of the chromosome is determined by the position of centromere on the chromosome. Chromosomes may be of following five types on the basis of their shape. (i) Acentric- Centromere remains absent. (ii)Telocentric- Centromere present at one end of chromosome. (iii)Acrocentric- When chromosome is divided into a very small segment at one end and a very large segment on the other end. (iv)Submetacentric- When chromosome have two unequal segments, one of which is slightly larger than other and forms L-shaped chromosome. (v)Metacentric- When two segments are equal and forming $V$-shaped structure.

45118.subject: Botany
45118.text: Induction of flowering by low temperature treatment is
45118.sol: Vernalization is chilling or cold treatment of the young plants or seeds to induce flowering. It is a process of shortening of the juvenile or vegetative phase and fastening the flowering by a process of cold treatment. It was first reported by a Russion worker, Lysenko (1928) while working on cold requiring biennial plants. Common examples of plants requiring vernalization are winter rye, winter wheat, winter barley, pea, Chrysanthemum etc.Cryobiology is the study of life at low temperature, usually at liquid nitrogen (ie $-196^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ) and preservation of organisms in liquid by chemical methods.Photoperiodism is the effect of photoperiods or daily duration of light hours (and dark periods) on the growth and development mainly flowering in plants. It was first studied by 'Garner and Allard' (1920) on 'Maryland Mammoth' variety of tobacco.

Thus, in (i) $\mathrm{O}_2$-act as oxidising agent (oxidise sulphide to $\mathrm{SO}_2$ ) and in (ii) Zn act as reducing agent (reduce $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}$to Ag ).

46310.text:
A skier starts from rest at point $A$ and slides down the hill without turning or breaking. The friction coefficient is $\mu$. When he stops at point $B$, his horizontal displacement is $S$. What is the height difference between points $A$ and $B ?$
(The velocity of the skier is small so that the additional pressure on the snow due to the curvature can be neglected. Neglect also the friction of air and the dependence of $\mu$ on the velocity of the skier.)
46310.sol: According to question, the situation is shown in the figure For a sufficiently safe-horizontal displacement $\Delta S$ can be considered straight. If the corresponding length of path element is $\Delta L$, the friction force is given by $\mu_{m g} \frac{\Delta S}{\Delta L}$ and the work done by the friction force equals force times displacement $\mu_{m g} \frac{\Delta S}{\Delta L} \Delta L=\mu_{m g} \Delta S$ Adding up, we find that along the whole path the total work done by the friction force is $\mu_{m g} s$. By energy conservation this must equals the decrease mgh in potential energy of skier. Hence, $h=\mu S$

Equation of wave
$y=5 \sin \left(\frac{t}{0.04}-\frac{x}{4}\right)$
The standard equation of a wave in the given form is
$y=a \sin \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$
Comparing the given equation with the standard equation, we get
$a=5 \text{ and } \omega=\frac{1}{0.04}=25$
Therefore, maximum velocity of particles of the medium,
$v_{\max }=a \omega=5 \times 25=125 \mathrm{cms}^{-1}=1.25 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$

\Rightarrow & & 3 x^{2}-4 x^{2}-4+8 x &=12 \\
\Rightarrow & &-x^{2}+8 x-16 &=0 \\
\Rightarrow & & x^{2}-8 x+16 &=0 \\
\Rightarrow & &x-4)^{2} &=0 \\

y &=3 \\

A ribonucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base attached to the ribose sugar at the C1' carbon via an N-glycosidic bond.

The β-D-ribofuranose form of ribose contains hydroxyl groups at positions C1', C2', C3', and C5'. During nucleoside formation, the hydroxyl at C1' is replaced by the nitrogenous base, leaving hydroxyl groups at C2', C3', and C5'.

$\boxed{3}$

55984.subject: Chemistry
55984.text: Which of the following reactions has of overall order $1.5$ ?
55984.sol:
The thermal decomposition of acetaldehyde is a well-known example of a reaction with a fractional order.

The reaction is: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}_{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_{4(g)} + \text{CO}_{(g)}$

The experimentally determined rate law for this reaction is:

$\text{Rate} = k[\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}]^{1.5}$

Thus, the overall order of the reaction is $1.5$.

For the other reactions:
$\text{H}_{2(g)} + \text{I}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{HI}_{(g)}$ follows second-order kinetics.
$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(\ell)} + \text{O}_{2(g)}$ follows first-order kinetics.
$2\text{NO}_{(g)} + 2\text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{N}_{2(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(\ell)}$ follows third-order kinetics.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}_{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_{4(g)} + \text{CO}_{(g)}$

56859.sol:
Cell emf calculation using Nernst equation

The cell reaction is: $\mathrm{Ni}_{(s)} + 2\mathrm{Ag}^{+}_{(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ni}^{+2}_{(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Ag}_{(s)}$ with $n = 2$ electrons transferred.

The reaction quotient is $Q = \frac{[\mathrm{Ni}^{+2}]}{[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}]^2} = \frac{0.01}{(0.01)^2} = 100$.

Applying the Nernst equation at 298 K:
$E_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.0592}{n} \log Q = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.0592}{2} \log 100 = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} - 0.0592 \mathrm{V}$

The cell emf is therefore less than the standard cell potential by $0.0592 \mathrm{V}$, matching option A.

58464.text: Identify the polymer used to obtain LCD screen from following.
58464.sol:
Polycarbonate is commonly used in the production of LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) screens, primarily because it is a durable, transparent plastic with excellent optical properties. Polycarbonate is used to make the outer layers of the screen or protective covers due to its high impact resistance and clarity.
Here's a brief overview of the other options:
- (A) Polyacrylamide: Used mainly in water treatment, paper production, and as a thickening agent; not typically used in LCDs.
- (B) Buna-N: A synthetic rubber (nitrile rubber) used for making seals, gaskets, and fuel hoses; not used in LCDs.
- (D) Perspex: Also known as acrylic, it's a transparent plastic, but it's more commonly used in optical devices, displays, and lenses rather than LCD screens.

60735.subject: Mathematics
60735.text: The locus of point of intersection of the tangents to the circle $x^2+y^2=16$, such that the angle between them is $60^{{}^{\circ}}$, is
60735.sol:
The circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$ has center at the origin and radius $4$. For two tangents from an external point $P(h, k)$ intersecting at $60^{}^{\circ}$, the line from the center to $P$ bisects the angle between the tangents, making the angle between $OP$ and either tangent $30^{}^{\circ}$.

In right triangle $\triangle OTP$, where $T$ is the point of tangency, $\sin 30^{}^{\circ} = \frac{r}{OP} = \frac{4}{OP}$. Since $\sin 30^{}^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}$, we have $OP = 8$.

The distance $OP = \sqrt{h^2 + k^2} = 8$, so squaring both sides yields $h^2 + k^2 = 64$. Replacing $(h, k)$ with $(x, y)$ gives the locus $x^2 + y^2 = 64$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

64427.subject: Mathematics
64427.text: The angle between lines whose direction cosines satisfy the equation $\ell+m+n=0$ and $\ell^2-m^2-n^2=0$, is
64427.sol:
The direction cosines $(\ell, m, n)$ satisfy $\ell + m + n = 0$ and $\ell^2 - m^2 - n^2 = 0$.

From the first equation, $n = -(\ell + m)$. Substituting into the second equation:

$\ell^2 - m^2 - (\ell+m)^2 = 0 \implies -2m^2 - 2\ell m = 0 \implies -2m(m+\ell) = 0$

Two cases emerge from this equation.

Case 1: $m = 0$

From $\ell + m + n = 0$ and m = 0, we find $\ell = -n$. Using the identity $\ell^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1$ yields $2n^2 = 1$, so $n = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.
One solution gives direction cosines $\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 0, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$.

Case 2: $\ell = -m$

From $\ell + m + n = 0$ and $\ell = -m$, we find $n = 0$. The identity becomes $2m^2 = 1$, so $m = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.
One solution gives direction cosines $\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 0\right)$.

The angle $\theta$ between these lines is given by:

$\cos \theta = |\ell_1 \ell_2 + m_1 m_2 + n_1 n_2| = \left| \left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + 0\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot 0 \right| = \frac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $\theta = rccos\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

65063.text: If $\bar{a}$, $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ are three vectors such that $|\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c}| = 1$, $\bar{c} = \lambda(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})$ and $|\bar{a}| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, $|\bar{b}| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $|\bar{c}| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$, then the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is
65063.sol:
Given $|\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c}| = 1$, squaring both sides gives:

$|\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2 + 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} + \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} + \bar{c} \cdot \bar{a}) = 1$

Since $\bar{c} = \lambda(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})$, the vector $\bar{c}$ is perpendicular to both $\bar{a} and \bar{b}$.

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = 0$ and $\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = 0$

Substituting the given magnitudes $|\bar{a}| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, $|\bar{b}| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, and $|\bar{c}| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$:

$\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\right)^2 + 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} + 0 + 0) = 1$

$\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{6} + 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) = 1$

$\dfrac{2 + 3 + 1}{6} + 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) = 1$

$1 + 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) = 1$

$2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) = 0$

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = 0$

$|\bar{a}| |\bar{b}| \cos \theta = 0$

Since $|\bar{a}| \neq 0$ and $|\bar{b}| \neq 0$, we have $\cos \theta = 0$.

$\theta = \dfrac{\pi^c}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi^c}{2}$

65890.subject: Physics
65890.text: When the electron orbiting in hydrogen atom goes from one orbit to another orbit (principal quantum number $=n$ ), the de-Broglie wavelength $(\lambda)$ associated with it is related to n as
65890.sol:
The relationship between the de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ and principal quantum number $n$ for an electron in a hydrogen atom follows from Bohr's quantization condition and the de Broglie hypothesis.

The angular momentum quantization requires $mvr = n\frac{h}{2\pi}$, where $m$ denotes electron mass, $v$ orbital velocity, $r$ orbital radius, and $h$ Planck's constant.

The de Broglie wavelength is given by $\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}$.

Substituting $mv = \frac{nh}{2\pi r}$ from the quantization condition yields $\lambda = \frac{2\pi r}{n}$, establishing $\lambda \propto \frac{r}{n}$.

Since the Bohr radius scales as $r_n = n^2 a_0$, combining these relations gives $\lambda \propto n$.

$\lambda$ is directly proportional to $n$.

66048.text: The capacitance of a capacitor becomes $\dfrac{7}{6}$ times the original value if dielectric slab of thickness $t = \dfrac{2d}{3}$ is introduced between the plates, where 'd' is the distance of separation between the plates. The dielectric constant of the slab is
66048.sol:
The initial capacitance of the capacitor is given by:

$C_0 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$

When a dielectric slab of thickness $t$ and dielectric constant $K$ is introduced, the new capacitance becomes:

$C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d - t + \dfrac{t}{K}}$

Substituting $t = \dfrac{2d}{3}$ into the expression:

$C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d - \dfrac{2d}{3} + \dfrac{2d}{3K}}$

$C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{\dfrac{d}{3} + \dfrac{2d}{3K}} = \dfrac{3 \epsilon_0 A}{d \left(1 + \dfrac{2}{K}\right)}$

$C = \dfrac{3 C_0}{1 + \dfrac{2}{K}}$

Given that $C = \dfrac{7}{6} C_0$, we can equate the two expressions:

$\dfrac{7}{6} = \dfrac{3}{1 + \dfrac{2}{K}}$

$7 \left(1 + \dfrac{2}{K}\right) = 18$

$7 + \dfrac{14}{K} = 18$

$\dfrac{14}{K} = 11$

$K = \dfrac{14}{11}$

Answer: $\dfrac{14}{11}$

68135.text: Two rain drops of same radius '$r$' falling with same terminal velocity '$V$' merge and form bigger drop of radius '$R$'. The terminal velocity of big drop is
68135.sol:
The terminal velocity of a spherical drop of radius $r$ falling through a viscous medium is given by Stokes' law:

$V = \dfrac{2}{9} \dfrac{r^2 (\rho - \sigma) g}{\eta}$

From this relation, the terminal velocity is directly proportional to the square of the radius of the drop:

$V \propto r^2$

For the smaller drop of radius $r$, the terminal velocity is $V$.

For the bigger drop of radius $R$, let the terminal velocity be $V'$.

Taking the ratio of their terminal velocities:

$\dfrac{V'}{V} = \dfrac{R^2}{r^2}$

$V' = \dfrac{V R^2}{r^2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{VR^2}{r^2}$

68443.text: A car passes three points A, B and C at $3$ m/s, $6$ m/s and $9$ m/s respectively in a straight line with uniform acceleration. If distance $AB = 60$ m then find the distance BC.
68443.sol:
Using the equation of motion $v^2 - u^2 = 2as$ for the interval AB:

$v_B^2 - v_A^2 = 2a(AB)$

$6^2 - 3^2 = 2a(60)$

$36 - 9 = 120a$

$27 = 120a \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{27}{120} = \dfrac{9}{40}$ m/s$^2$

Applying the same equation for the interval BC:

$v_C^2 - v_B^2 = 2a(BC)$

$9^2 - 6^2 = 2 \times \dfrac{9}{40} \times BC$

$81 - 36 = \dfrac{9}{20} \times BC$

$45 = \dfrac{9}{20} \times BC$

$BC = \dfrac{45 \times 20}{9} = 100$ m

Answer: $100$ m

68694.text: A mass 'M' attached to a horizontal spring executes S.H.M. of amplitude $A_1$. When the mass $M$ passes through its mean position, then a smaller mass ' m ' is placed over it and both of them move together with amplitude $A_2$. The ratio $\left(\frac{A_1}{A_2}\right)$ is
68694.sol:
Solution: Let the spring constant be $k$, with initial angular frequency $\omega_1 = \sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}$ for mass $M$ oscillating with amplitude $A_1$.

The maximum velocity at mean position is $v_1 = A_1 \omega_1 = A_1 \sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}$.

When mass $m$ is added at mean position, momentum conservation yields $(M + m)v_2 = M v_1$, so the new maximum velocity becomes $v_2 = \frac{M}{M + m} v_1$.

The new angular frequency is $\omega_2 = \sqrt{\frac{k}{M + m}}$, and the corresponding maximum velocity is $v_2 = A_2 \omega_2 = A_2 \sqrt{\frac{k}{M + m}}$.

Equating expressions for $v_2$: $A_2 \sqrt{\frac{k}{M + m}} = \frac{M}{M + m} A_1 \sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}$.

Simplifying and solving for the amplitude ratio: $A_2 = A_1 \frac{M}{\sqrt{M}\sqrt{M + m}}$, so $\frac{A_1}{A_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M + m}{M}}$.

This corresponds to option C.

68967.text: A concave lens (refractive index $=1 \cdot 5$) has both surfaces of same radius of curvature $R$. If it is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1 \cdot 75$ it will act as a
options: concave lens of focal length (3.5) R
concave lens of focal length 2 R
convex lens of focal length (3.5) R
convex lens of focal length 2 R
68967.sol:
The behavior of a biconcave lens immersed in a liquid depends on the relative refractive indices. Given the lens material index $n_L = 1.5$ and the liquid medium index $n_M = 1.75$, the lens maker's formula yields the focal length.

For a biconcave lens with equal radii of curvature $R$, the radii are $R_1 = -R$ and $R_2 = +R$ by standard sign convention. Substituting into the formula:

$\frac{1}{f} = \left(\frac{n_L}{n_M} - 1\right) \left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right) =\left(\frac{1.5}{1.75} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{-R} - \frac{1}{R}\right)

The refractive index term simplifies as \frac{1.5}{1.75} -1 = -\frac{1}{7}, and the curvature term is \frac{1}{-R} - \frac{1}{R} = -\frac{2}{R}. Multiplying these gives:

\frac{1}{f} = \left(-\frac{1}{7}\right) \left(-\frac{2}{R}\right) = \frac{2}{7R}

Thus, $ f = $\frac{7R}{2} =3.5R$. The positive focal length indicates the lens is converging, acting as a convex lens.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{L}{9}$

70491.text: Two identical straight wires are stretched so as to produce 6 beats per second when vibrating simultaneously with tensions ' $\mathrm{T}_1$ ' and ' $\mathrm{T}_2$ ' respectively. On changing the tension slightly in one of them, the beat frequency remains unchanged. This will happen when (Given $\rightarrow \mathrm{T}_1 > \mathrm{T}_2$ )
70491.sol:
Problem Analysis: Given two identical wires with initial tensions $T_1 > T_2$, the frequencies satisfy $f_1 = C \sqrt{T_1}$ and $f_2 = C \sqrt{T_2}$, where $C$ is a constant. The 6 Hz beat frequency implies $f_1 - f_2 = 6$.

Altering tension slightly while maintaining the beat frequency at 6 Hz implies a crossover in frequencies. If $T_1$ is changed, the frequency must decrease such that $f_1' = f_2 - 6$, requiring $T_1$ to be decreased. If $T_2$ is changed, the frequency must increase such that $f_2' = f_1 + 6$, requiring $T_2$ to be increased.

The only consistent option is to decrease $T_1$ or increase $T_2$, matching choice D. The specific tension change magnitude (144) is irrelevant as only direction matters for the beat frequency to remain unchanged. The correct option is $\boxed{D}$.

71943.subject: Chemistry
71943.text: The volume of fcc unit cell is $5.6\times10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$. Calculate the molar mass of metal if the density of metal is $20.4\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$. [N_A=6.022\times10^{23}$]$
71943.sol:
The density of a unit cell is given by the formula:

$d = \dfrac{Z \times M}{N_A \times V}$

For an fcc unit cell, the number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 4$.

Rearranging the formula to solve for molar mass $M$:

$M = \dfrac{d \times N_A \times V}{Z}$

Substituting the given values:

$M = \dfrac{20.4 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 5.6 \times 10^{-23}}{4}$

$M = \dfrac{20.4 \times 6.022 \times 5.6}{4}$

$M = 171.98 \approx 172\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $172\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

72183.subject: Physics
72183.text: A conducting rod AB is in contact with metal rails AC and BD, which are $0.25$ m apart in a uniform magnetic field of induction $0.4$ T acting perpendicular to the plane of the figure. Ends C and D are connected through a $5\ \Omega$ resistor. If the rod AB moves to right with a velocity of $5$ m/s, then the magnitude and direction of the current through rod AB is
72183.sol:
The motional emf induced in the moving rod is given by:
$E = Bvl$

Substituting the given values ($B = 0.4\text{ T}$, $v = 5\text{ m/s}$, $l = 0.25\text{ m}$):
$E = 0.4 \times 5 \times 0.25 = 0.5\text{ V}$

The magnitude of the induced current is:
$I = \dfrac{E}{R}$
$I = \dfrac{0.5}{5} = 0.1\text{ A}$

The direction of the induced current can be determined using Fleming's Right-Hand Rule or the Lorentz force on positive charges ($\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$).
With velocity $\vec{v}$ towards the right and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ into the plane of the paper, the force on positive charges is directed upwards.
Therefore, the induced current in the rod AB flows from B to A.

Answer: $0.1$ A from B to A

72471.subject: Physics
72471.text: For the given wave equation $y = 10\cos\pi\left(\dfrac{x}{4} + \dfrac{t}{2}\right)$, the CORRECT statement is ( where x is in metre and time t is in second.)
72471.sol:
The given wave equation is $y = 10\cos\pi\left(\dfrac{x}{4} + \dfrac{t}{2}\right)$

Rewriting the equation, we get $y = 10\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}t\right)$

Comparing with the standard wave equation $y = A\cos(kx + \omega t)$, we get:

Angular frequency $\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\ \text{rad/s}$

Wave number $k = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\ \text{m}^{-1}$

Frequency $f = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi} = \dfrac{\pi/2}{2\pi} = 0.25\ \text{Hz}$

Wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi}{k} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\pi/4} = 8\ \text{m}$

Wave velocity $v = f\lambda = 0.25 \times 8 = 2\ \text{m/s} = 200\ \text{cm/s}$

Thus, the only correct statement is frequency $= 0.25\ \text{Hz}$.

Answer: frequency $= 0.25\ \text{Hz}$

72505.subject: Physics
72505.text: An organ pipe $p_1$ closed at one end has vibrating air column in its first overtone and another pipe $P_2$ open at both ends has vibrating air column in the third overtone, are in resonance with a given tuning fork. The ratio of the length of pipe $P_1$ to that of $P_2$ is
72505.sol:
For pipe $P_1$ (closed at one end), the frequency of the first overtone corresponds to the third harmonic. Its frequency is given by:

$f_1 = \dfrac{3v}{4L_1}$

For pipe $P_2$ (open at both ends), the frequency of the third overtone corresponds to the fourth harmonic. Its frequency is given by:

$f_2 = \dfrac{4v}{2L_2}$

Since both pipes are in resonance with the same tuning fork, their frequencies must be equal:

$f_1 = f_2$

$\dfrac{3v}{4L_1} = \dfrac{4v}{2L_2}$

$\dfrac{3}{4L_1} = \dfrac{2}{L_2}$

$\dfrac{L_1}{L_2} = \dfrac{3}{8}$

The ratio of the length of pipe $P_1$ to that of $P_2$ is $3 : 8$.

Answer: $3 : 8$

72507.sol:

For the third overtone, $p=3$.

Number of nodes $= 3 + 1 = 4$

Number of antinodes $= 3 + 1 = 4$

Thus, the air column has four nodes and four antinodes.

Answer: four nodes and four antinodes

74225.text: Which one of the following statements about sound is NOT correct?
options: Sound travels at a speed slower than the speed of light
Sound travels faster in moist air than in dry air
74225.sol:
The sensation felt by our ears is called sound. It is a form of energy which makes us hear. Sound travels in the form of wave.
Longitudinal Waves: A wave in which the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth in the 'same direction' in which the wave is moving. Medium can be solid, liquid or gases. Therefore, sound waves are longitudinal waves. Sound is a longitudinal wave which consists of compressions and rarefactions travelling through a medium.
Transverse Waves: A wave in which the particles of the medium vibrate up and down 'at right angles' to the direction in which the wave is moving. These waves are produced only in a solids and liquids but not in gases.

76791.subject: Mathematics
76791.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $f(x) = [x^2]$, where $[\cdot]$ is the greatest integer function.

What is $\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} f(x) \, dx$ equal to?
76791.sol:
The given integral is $\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} [x^2] \, dx$.

As $x$ varies from $\sqrt{2} to 2$, $x^2$ varies from $2 to 4$. The greatest integer function $[x^2]$ changes its value when $x^2$ is an integer. The integer values of $x^2$ in this interval are $2, 3, and 4$, which correspond to $x = \sqrt{2}, \sqrt{3}, and 2$.

We split the integral at $x = \sqrt{3}$:

For $x \in (\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{3})$, $2 < x^2 < 3 \Rightarrow [x^2] = 2$

For $x \in (\sqrt{3}, 2)$, $3 < x^2 < 4 \Rightarrow [x^2] = 3$

The integral can be written as:

\$int_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} [$x^2] \, dx = \$int_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}$2 \, dx + \$int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}$3 \, dx

Evaluating the $integrals:

\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}} 2 \, dx = 2[x]_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}} = 2(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}) = 2\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{2}$

$\int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2} 3 \, dx = 3[x]_{\sqrt{3}}^{2} = 3(2 - \sqrt{3}) = 6 - 3\sqrt{3}$

Adding the two values:

$\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} [x^2] \, dx = (2\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{2}) + (6 - 3\sqrt{3})$

$\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} [x^2] \, dx = 6 - \sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{2}$

Answer: $6 - \sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{2}

Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1}$, where $x \neq 2n\pi$ and $n$ is an integer.

What is the range of the function?
77296.sol:
Given function is $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{1 - \cos x}$

The range of $\cos x$ is $[-1, 1]$.

Since $x \neq 2n\pi$, $\cos x \neq 1$.

Therefore, $-1 \le \cos x < 1$

Multiplying by $-1$, we get $-1 < -\cos x \le 1$

Adding $1$, we get $0 < 1 - \cos x \le 2$

Taking the reciprocal, we get $\dfrac{1}{1 - \cos x} \ge \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, $y \ge 0.5$

The range of the function is $[0.5, \infty)$.

78179.sol:
Converting the given binary numbers to decimal:

$x = (1111)_2 = 1 \times 2^3 + 1 \times 2^2 + 1 \times 2^1 + 1 \times 2^0 = 15$

$y = (1001)_2 = 1 \times 2^3 + 0 \times 2^2 + 0 \times 2^1 + 1 \times 2^0 = 9$

$z = (110)_2 = 1 \times 2^2 + 1 \times 2^1 + 0 \times 2^0 = 6$

Observing the relationship between $x$, $y$, and $z$:

$y + z = 9 + 6 = 15 = x$

$\Rightarrow x - y - z = 0$

Using the algebraic identity, if $a + b + c = 0$, then $a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc = 0$.

Substituting $a = x$, $b = -y$, and $c = -z$:

$x + (-y) + (-z) = 0$

$\Rightarrow x^3 + (-y)^3 + (-z)^3 - 3(x)(-y)(-z) = 0$

$\Rightarrow x^3 - y^3 - z^3 - 3xyz = 0$

In binary representation, $0$ is $(0)_2$.

Answer: $(0)_2$

Question: Consider the following: 1. The coordinates of $Q$ are $(4,-3,-1)$. 2. PQ is of length more than 8 units. 3. The point $(1,-1,-3)$ is the mid-point of the line segment PQ and lies on the given plane. Which of the above statements are correct?

The Equation of line $P Q$ is $\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y-1}{-2}=\frac{z+5}{2}=$ r$ Coordinates of any point on the line $P Q$ is 3 r-2,-2 r+ 1 and 2 r-5$.
Let $Q(3 r-2,-2 r+1,2 r-5)$ be such a point.
Let $L$ be the mid point of $P Q, L= \left(\frac{3 r}{2}-2,1-r, r-5\right)$
Since $L$ lies on the plane $3 x-2 y+2 z+1=0$
So, $3\left(\frac{3 r}{2}-2\right)$-2(1-r)+2(r-5)+1=0\Rightarrow $\frac{17}{2}$ r-17=0 \Rightarrow r=2$
So, coordinates of $Q$ are $(3 \times2-2,-2 \times2+1,2 \times2-5)=(4,-3,-1)$...(ii)
Also the mid point of $P Q$ is $L=$\left(\frac{3 \times 2}{2}-2,1-2,2-5\right)=$(1,-1,-3)$...(iii)
\begin{aligned}
& \therefore P Q=\sqrt{(-2-4)^2+(1+3)^2+(-5+1)^2}=\sqrt{68}\\
& \Rightarrow P Q=2 \sqrt{17} >8
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Option (4) is correct.

80010.text: The oxygen evolved during photosynthesis comes from water molecules. Which one of the following pairs of elements is involved in this reaction?
80010.sol:
During non-cyclic photophosphorylation, the PS-II helps in the photolysis of water molecules which evolves oxygen as a by-product. For the photolysis of water, some cations (like $M{g}^{+ 2}andM{n}^{+ 2}$) and anions (like $C{l}^{-}$) are involved. The proton generated in this process is used to make the proton gradient for ATP synthesis.

Manganese, chlorine, and calcium help in the photolysis of water during the light reaction of photosynthesis.

80149.subject: Botany
80149.text: The enzyme required for carboxylation in the Calvin cycle is :
80149.sol:
The Calvin cycle is the primary pathway for carbon fixation in plants.

The first step of the Calvin cycle is carboxylation, where carbon dioxide is added to a five-carbon acceptor molecule, Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP).

This reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase, commonly known as RuBisCO.

Hexokinase is an enzyme involved in glycolysis.

PEP carboxylase is the primary carboxylating enzyme in the C4 pathway.

Carboxypeptidase is a proteolytic enzyme involved in digestion.

Answer: RuBP carboxylase – oxygenase

80150.subject: Botany
80150.text: Select the correct sequence of experiments that led to a gradual understanding of photosynthesis in green plants.
options: Production of glucose $\rightarrow$ role of air $\rightarrow$ release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b $\rightarrow$ production of glucose $\rightarrow$ release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ role of air
Role of air $\rightarrow$ release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ production of glucose $\rightarrow$ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ production of glucose $\rightarrow$ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b $\rightarrow$ role of air
80150.sol:
Joseph Priestley (1770) performed experiments that revealed the essential role of air in the growth of green plants.

Jan Ingenhousz (1779) showed that sunlight is essential to the plant process and that only the green parts of the plants release oxygen.

Julius von Sachs (1854) provided evidence for the production of glucose when plants grow.

T.W. Engelmann (1843-1909) described the first action spectrum of photosynthesis, which roughly resembles the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b.

The correct chronological sequence is role of air $\rightarrow$ release of oxygen $\rightarrow$ production of glucose $\rightarrow$ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b.

80451.subject: Botany
options: triose phosphate is the electron donor while acetaldehyde is the electron acceptor
triose phosphate is the electron donor while pyruvic acid is the electron acceptor
80451.sol:
During fermentation, glucose undergoes glycolysis and yields pyruvic acid, which then transformed into acetyl CoA. Then glyceraldehyde phosphate is produced, which then transforms to acetaldehyde and this acetaldehyde transforms into ethanol. In alcohol fermentation triose phosphate is the electron donor, at the same time as acetaldehyde is the electron acceptor.
Related Theory
Alcoholic fermentation is also known as ethanol fermentation where biological elements such as glucose, fructose, and sucrose are converted into cellular energy and thereby produce ethanol and carbon dioxide as their by-product.

82315.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
82315.text: A ball moving with velocity $2 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ collides head on with another stationary ball of double the mass. If the coefficient of restitution is 0.5 , then their velocities (in $\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ ) after collision will be
82315.sol:
If two bodies collide head on with coefficient of restitution

$\mathrm{e}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_2-\mathrm{v}_1}{\mathrm{u}_1-\mathrm{u}_2}$ From the law of conservation of linear momentum

$\begin{array}{r}\mathrm{m}_{1}  \mathrm{u}$}_{1}+$\mathrm{m}_{2}  \mathrm{u}$}_{2}=$\mathrm{m}_{1}  \mathrm{v}$}_{1}+$\mathrm{m}_{2}  \mathrm{v}$}_{2} \\
\Rightarrow \quad $\mathrm{v}_{1}=\left[\frac{\mathrm{m}_1-\mathrm{em}_2}{\mathrm{ m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2}\right] \mathrm{u}$}_{1}+$\left[\frac{(1+\mathrm{e}) \mathrm{m}_2}{\mathrm{ m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2}\right] \mathrm{u}_{2}
\end{array}

Substituting \mathrm{u}_1=2 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}, \mathrm{u}_2=0, \mathrm{ m}_1=\mathrm{m} and

\mathrm{m}$}_{2}=2 $\mathrm{ m}, \mathrm{e}=0.5

we get

\begin{array}{lc}\text{ we get }$& $\mathrm{v}_{1}=\left[\frac{\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{m}+2 \mathrm{ m}}\right] \times2 \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{v}$}_{1}=0
\end{array}

Similarly,

$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{v}_{2} & =\left[\frac{(1+\mathrm{e}) \mathrm{m}_1}{\mathrm{ m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2}\right] \mathrm{u}$}_{1}+\$ left[\frac{\mathrm{m}_2-\mathrm{em}_1}{\mathrm{ m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2}\right] \mathrm{u} }_{2} \\
& $=\$left[\frac{1.5 \times \mathrm{m}}{3 \mathrm{ m}}\right] \times$$2 \\
& =1 $\mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$$
\end{aligned}$$

83605.sol:
Loss of heat by the hot body = gain of heat by the cold body.

Since, the heat capacity increases with temperature, the hotter body will lose more energy when its temperature falls down from $100{}^{o}C$ to $50{}^{o}C$ compared to the energy required by the cold body to raise its temperature from $0{}^{o}C$ to $50{}^{o}C$. 84689.subject: Zoology
84689.text: In the human female, menstruation can be deferred by the administration of:
84689.sol:
The progesterone and oestradiol continue the hypertrophy of endometrial lining in the uterus and fallopian tubes and maintain it throughout pregnancy. progesterone is also necessary for the proper implantation of the foetus in the uterine wall. It stimulates the endometrial glands to secrete a nutrient fluid for the foetus, hence the term secretory phase. The progesterone inhibits the release of FSH so that it may not develop additional follicles and eggs.
Related Theory
There is no menstrual cycle during pregnancy due to the secretion of progesterone hormone by the corpus luteum. The progesterone hormone inhibits the production of the gonadotropic hormones from the pituitary and prevents the uterine lining from sloughing and supports pregnancy.

92189.text: Let the equation of a line is $\dfrac{x - 2}{1} = \dfrac{y - 3}{2} = \dfrac{z - 4}{3}$. An insect starts flying from $P  \left(1, 3, 2\right)$ in a straight line meeting the given line at a point $R  \left(a, b, c\right)$ and then goes to the point $Q  \left(6, 7, 5\right)$ in a straight line such that $PR$ is perpendicular to $RQ.$ Then, the least value of $7  \left($ a + b + c\right)$ is equal to$
92189.sol:
Any general point on the line is $\left(\lambda + 2, 2\lambda + 3, \lambda + 4\right)$

$\overset{→}{PR} = < \lambda + 1, 2\lambda, 3\lambda + 2 >$
$\overset{→}{RQ} = < 4 - \lambda, 4 - 2\lambda, 1 - 3\lambda >$

$⇒ \left(\lambda + 1\right)\left(4 - \lambda\right) + 2\lambda\left(4 - 2\lambda\right) + \left(3\lambda + 2\right)\left(1 - 3\lambda\right) = 0$
$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} - 3\lambda - 4 + 4{\lambda}^{2} - 8\lambda + 9{\lambda}^{2} + 3\lambda - 2 = 0$
$⇒ 14{\lambda}^{2} - 8\lambda - 6 = 0$
$⇒ \lambda = 1, - \dfrac{3}{7}$
Coordinates of $R$~are& $\left(3, 5, 7\right)$ or $\left(\dfrac{11}{7}, \dfrac{15}{7}, \dfrac{19}{7}\right)$
Least value of $7\left(a + b + c\right) = 11 + 15 + 19 = 45$

options: Head, muscular foot and visceral hump
95526.sol:
Phylum Mollusca:
This is the second largest animal phylum. Molluscs are terrestrial or aquatic (marine or freshwater) having an organ-system level of organisation. They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and coelomate animals. Body is covered by a calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump. A soft and spongy layer of skin forms a mantle over the visceral hump. The space between the hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity in which feather-like gills are present. They have respiratory and excretory functions. The anterior head region has sensory tentacles. The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

Examples: Pila (Apple snail), Pinctada (Pearl oyster), Sepia& (Cuttlefish), Loligo (Squid), Octopus (Devil fish), Aplysia (Seahare), Dentalium (Tusk shell) and Chaetopleura (Chiton).

95815.text:
Match Column-I with Column - II and select the CORRECT option from the codes given below.
&
& Column I & Column II
1 Phycomycetes i Sac fungi
2 Ascomycetes ii Algal fungi
3 Basidiomycetes iii Fungi imperfecti
4 Deuteromycetes iv Fungi imperfecti
95815.sol:
Fungi form a unique group of heterotrophic organisms showing wide diversity. Based various features like spore formation mode, fruiting bodies fungi is categorized into -

Phycomycetes - Mainly aquatic habitat, also seen growing on decaying wood. Their mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. Zoospores or aplanosopres are formed during asexual reproduction. Mucor, Rhizopus, Albugo are included in this group.

Ascomycetes - Majorly multi cellular and also called sac-fungi as their reproductive spores are produced in sac like structure called ascus. For asexual reproduction, conidia are produced in specialized structure called conidiophore. This group includes Penicillium, Aspergillus, Claviceps.

Basidiomycetes - Filamentous fungi having hyphae and specialized club-shaped cells called basidia involved in sexual reproduction. Agaricus(Mushroom), Puccinia, Ustilago fall in this group.

Deuteromycetes - Reproduce only via asexual mode through spores called conidia. The mycelium of this group is septate and branched. Trichoderma, Colletotrichum are included in this group.

97934.subject: Botany
97934.text:
Consider the following:

i. For a solution at atmospheric pressure ${Ψ}_{w}$ = ${Ψ}_{s}$
ii. ${Ψ}_{w}$ (water potential) of a cell is affected by solute potential only
iii. ${Ψ}_{p}$ (pressure potential) is usually positive in xylem during the day

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
97934.sol: Water potential of a solution is the sum total of four components: gravitational potential, osmotic(solute) potential, matric potential and pressure potential. But, since matric potential and gravitational potential are negligible, water potential is generally more affected by solute and pressure potential. Pressure potential of water during the standard stage is 0 MPa. The positive value of water potential within the cell is referred to as turgor pressure. During the day when transpiration is high, pressure potential of the xylem mostly is negative since water is evaporated and its turgor pressure is less.

101112.text:
Statement 1 Two cylinders, one hollow (metal) and the other solid (wood) with the same mass and identical dimensions are simultaneously allowed to roll without slipping down an inclined plane from the same height. The hollow cylinder will reach the bottom of the inclined plane first.

& \therefore \text{ correct option is }(\mathrm{d})
\end{aligned}$

101556.subject: Physics
101556.text: A uniform solid cylindrical rod is subjected to a longitudinal tensile stress. It is observed that its length increases by $0.1\%$ while its diameter decreases by $0.03\%$. The Poisson's ratio of the material of the rod is:
101556.sol:
Poisson's ratio ($\sigma$) is defined as the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain.

The longitudinal strain is the fractional change in length:
Longitudinal strain $= \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} = \dfrac{0.1}{100} = 0.001$

The lateral strain is the fractional change in diameter (considering magnitude):
Lateral strain $= \dfrac{\Delta d}{d} = \dfrac{0.03}{100} = 0.0003$

Poisson's ratio is given by:
$\sigma = \dfrac{\text{Lateral strain}}{\text{Longitudinal strain}} = \dfrac{0.0003}{0.001} = 0.3$

Alternatively, using percentage changes directly:
$\sigma = \dfrac{0.03\%}{0.1\%} = 0.3$

Answer: $0.3$

102413.subject: Physics
102413.text: A simple pendulum of length $l$ executes simple harmonic motion with a small angular amplitude $\theta_0$. What is the linear speed of the bob when its kinetic energy is equal to its potential energy? (Assume potential energy is zero at the mean position and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity)
102413.sol:
For a simple pendulum of length $l$ executing SHM with angular amplitude $\theta_0$, the linear amplitude is:
$A = l \theta_0$

The angular frequency of the simple pendulum is:
$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{l}}$

The total mechanical energy $E$ of the pendulum bob of mass $m$ is:
$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 A^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m \left(\dfrac{g}{l}\right) (l \theta_0)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m g l \theta_0^2$

When the kinetic energy $K$ is equal to the potential energy $U$, the kinetic energy is exactly half of the total energy:
$K = \dfrac{E}{2}$

Substituting the expressions for $K$ and $E$:
$\dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{2} m g l \theta_0^2 \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} m g l \theta_0^2$

$v^2 = \dfrac{g l \theta_0^2}{2}$

$v = \theta_0 \sqrt{\dfrac{g l}{2}}$

Answer: $\theta_0 \sqrt{\dfrac{g l}{2}}$

102430.subject: Physics
102430.text: Which of the following functions represents a periodic motion with a time period of $T = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$?
102430.sol:
A function represents periodic motion if it repeats its value after a regular interval of time, called the time period $T$. For a trigonometric function representing simple harmonic motion with angular frequency $\omega'$, the time period is given by $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega'}$.

Let us evaluate the time period for each option:
Option 1: $f(t) = \sin(\omega t) + \cos(\omega t) = \sqrt{2}\sin\left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$. The angular frequency is $\omega$, so the time period is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$.
Option 2: $f(t) = \sin\left(\dfrac{\omega t}{2}\right)$. The angular frequency is $\dfrac{\omega}{2}$, so the time period is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega/2} = \dfrac{4\pi}{\omega}$.
Option 3: $f(t) = e^{-2\omega t}$ is an exponentially decaying function. It does not repeat its values, so it represents a non-periodic motion.
Option 4: $f(t) = \sin(2\omega t) + \cos(2\omega t) = \sqrt{2}\sin\left(2\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$. The angular frequency is $2\omega$, so the time period is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{2\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$.

Thus, $\sin(2\omega t) + \cos(2\omega t)$ is the correct function.

Answer: $\sin(2\omega t) + \cos(2\omega t)$

102873.subject: Physics
102873.text: A hollow metal sphere of radius $R$ is uniformly charged. What is the ratio of the electric potential at a distance of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ from the centre to the electric potential at a distance of $2R$ from the centre?
102873.sol:
For a uniformly charged hollow metal sphere of radius $R$ and charge $Q$:

The electric potential at any point inside the sphere ($r < R$) is constant and equal to the potential at its surface. Therefore, at a distance $r = \dfrac{R}{2}$, the potential is:
$V_{\text{inside}} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{R}$

The electric potential at a point outside the sphere ($r > R$) is inversely proportional to the distance from the centre. At a distance $r = 2R$, the potential is:
$V_{\text{outside}} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{2R}$

Taking the ratio of the two potentials:
$\dfrac{V_{\text{inside}}}{V_{\text{outside}}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{R}}{\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{2R}} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 2$

Thus, the ratio is $2 : 1$.

Answer: $2 : 1$

103426.text: You are given resistance wire of length 50 cm and a battery of negligible resistance. In which of the following cases is largest amount of heat generated?
options: When the wire is connected to the battery directly
When the wire is divided into two parts and both the parts are connected to the battery in parallel.
When the wire is divided into four parts and all the four parts are connected to the battery in parallel.
When only half of the wire is connected to the battery.
103426.sol:
Let $R$ be the resistance of the wire
(a) $H_1=\frac{V^2 t}{R}$
(b) Resistance of each part will be $R$ / 2. When they are connected in parallel, the resistance will be $R / 4$.
Hence, $H_2=\frac{4 v^2 t}{R}$
(c) In case of four wires connected in parallel, the resistance will be $R$ / 8
$\therefore H_3=\frac{8 V^2 t}{R}$
(d) $H_4=\frac{V^2 t}{[R / 2]}=\frac{2 V^2 \cdot t}{R}$
Hence, largest amount of heat will be generated in case of four parts connected in parallel.

104627.subject: Physics
104627.text: A short linear object of length $b$ lies along the axis of a concave mirror of focal length $f$ at a distance $u$ from the pole of the mirror, what is the size of image?
104627.sol:
Using the relation for the focal length of concave mirror
$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}$ ...(1)
Differentiating equation (1), we obtain
$0=-\frac{1}{v^2} d v-\frac{1}{u^2} d u$
So, $\quad d v=-\frac{v^2}{u^2} \times b \ldots(2)$
(Here : $d u=b$ )
From equation (1)
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{v} & =\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{u-f}{f u} \\
\frac{u}{v} & =\frac{u-f}{f} \\
\end{aligned} \frac{v}{u}=\frac{f}{u-f} \ldots(3)$
Now, from equations (2) and (3), we get
$d v=-\left(\frac{f}{u-f}\right)^2 b$
Therefore, size or image is $=\left(\frac{f}{u-f}\right)^2 b$
